appliesToWhy: GA 3.1.1 and appendix B: the one push id held with two hands cupping one dumbbell.

handContact.text: Both palms against the inside of the top dumbbell head, the handle running between thumb and fingers.

thumbRule.text: Thumbs wrapped around the handle, fingers on the dumbbell head.

loadAxis.text: along-forearm: at the top the palms face up with the dumbbell hanging over the head, so the weight rests in the upturned palms.
loadAxis.basis: drawing decision for the lever check, read across from c4 (ACE's wrap-the-handle grip, palms up, dumbbell hanging over the head); not a sourced claim for the cupped grip

wrist.text: Keep the wrist position unchanged through the set.

alternative.text: Another way is both hands wrapped around the handle.

gripLine.text: Cup the top of one dumbbell with both palms, thumbs wrapped round the handle.

claims.text: Hold one dumbbell with both hands, thumbs wrapped round the handle and fingers gripping the body of the dumbbell.

quotes.text: Grip the Dumbbell: Hold a single dumbbell with both hands. Your thumbs should wrap around the handle and fingers grip the body of the dumbbell.

claims.text: Place the palms against the inside of the dumbbell head, with the handle running between thumb and finger; another source describes grasping the inside plate surface with both hands.

quotes.text: Place your palms against the inside of the dumbbell head. The handle should run between your thumb and finger.
Hold the weight overhead by grasping the inside dumbbell plate surface with both hands, or by grasping both handles of the kettlebell.

claims.text: An alternative grip wraps both hands around the dumbbell handle.

quotes.text: Stand in a split-stance position holding a dumbbell with both hands and wrap both hands around the dumbbell handle.

claims.text: At the top the dumbbell sits directly over the head with the palms facing up and the dumbbell hanging vertically or slightly angled.

quotes.text: The dumbbell should be positioned directly over your head with your palms facing upwards and the dumbbell hanging vertically or angled slightly.

claims.text: Keep the head, torso, upper arms, wrists and feet in the same position through the exercise.

quotes.text: Maintain your balance and avoid changing the position of your head, torso, upper arms, wrists and feet.

sources.title: Dumbbell Triceps Extension - How To, Muscles Worked & Form Guide (Liftosaur)
Overhead Triceps Extension (How To, Muscles Worked, & Variations) (Lift Big Eat Big, James de Lacey)
Overhead Tricep Extension: How-To and Variations (Healthline; Travis Edwards, PT)

gaps: No source read gives a wrist angle or names a hand fault for the cupped grip (for example the dumbbell tipping or the hands sliding off the head). No fault is drawn until one is sourced; GA's push faults (fingers-bent-back, ulnar-tip) are not carried over.
No source read says how to get the dumbbell overhead or down again for this grip (tier-A way out, LR-3, LR-13: stays with LIB-WAYOUT).
overBody: the dumbbell is over the head, so GA requires a wrapped thumb; c1 and c2 support thumbs round the handle, but no source states that a cupped grip keeps the dumbbell from falling.
notes: ACE (c3) and the cupped sources (c1, c2) describe two different grips. cards/dumbbell_overhead_triceps_extension.json cites ACE c1 (handle) and Healthline c2 (inside plate). This card makes the cupped grip the default per GA 3.1.1 and keeps the handle grip as the alternative; the sheet author picks one per plate.
loadAxis along-forearm is supported only as a reading of c4 (palms up, dumbbell hanging over the head); it is a drawing decision for the lever check, not a measured fact.
Re-read ACE triceps extension and Healthline in full on 2026-10-01; Liftosaur and Lift Big Eat Big are new here.
